heading: Explain async/await and how Task-based asynchrony works.
content: 'async' marks a method as asynchronous, allowing it to use 'await' on a Task without blocking the calling thread. While the awaited operation (I/O, a web call, etc.) is in flight, the thread is freed to do other work; when the operation completes, execution resumes roughly where it left off. This improves throughput for I/O-bound work -- it does not make CPU-bound code faster by itself.

heading: What are delegates and events, and how do they differ?
content: A delegate is a type-safe reference to a method -- essentially a function pointer with a signature. An event is built on top of a delegate but restricts who can invoke it: only the declaring class can raise it, while subscribers (outside the class) can only add or remove handlers. Events are the standard way to implement the publish/subscribe pattern safely.

heading: What is the difference between IEnumerable and IQueryable?
content: IEnumerable executes query operators in-memory on the client, once the data has already been pulled into a collection. IQueryable builds an expression tree that a provider (e.g. EF Core) translates into a query (e.g. SQL) and executes at the source, so filtering/sorting happens on the database before data is sent over the wire. Mixing them carelessly (e.g. calling .ToList() too early) is a common performance pitfall.
